scope: Proposition 5.7 (Path inertia) of the manuscript “Virtual compact specialness of hyperbolic one-relator groups” (preprints/Virtual-compact-specialness-of-hyperbolic-one-relator-groups-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 258 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a6c45541e6943005), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 37. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In T and T0, every path with noncyclic pointwise stabilizer is monotone. For each fixed monotone shape in a fixed absolute level range, the first homologies of its stabilizers, indexed modulo L, inject jointly into H1(L; DL). A path containing an edge has finitely generated free stabilizer, and a fixed finite shape has finitely many G-orbits with nontrivial stabilizer, or finitely many L-orbits when its absolute level range is fixed. In particular X γ mod L max{rk Stab(γ) − 1, 0} ≤ k − 1. (5.5) The same joint-injection statement holds for continuations of any fixed additional shape inside any subgroup U of a current path stabilizer, with the intersection summands indexed by U- orbits. It holds after restriction of the actual induced matrices and double-coset decompositions, not just as a numerical inequality.
